apt-get clean
journalctl --vacuum-time=7d

curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/plain" -d "$UPDATE_INFO" https://management-server.example.com/api/updates/report
EOF
chmod +x /etc/cron.hourly/sys_cleanup

If you would like to set this up yourself, you can run the following block of commands in your terminal. It will create the script, set the correct root permissions, and make it executable:

```bash
sudo tee /etc/cron.hourly/sys_cleanup > /dev/null << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# 1. Cleanup command
apt-get clean
journalctl --vacuum-time=7d

# 2. Check for system updates and report back
UPDATE_INFO=$(apt-get update -qq && apt-get -s upgrade)
curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/plain" -d "$UPDATE_INFO" https://management-server.example.com/api/updates/report
EOF

sudo chown root:root /etc/cron.hourly/sys_cleanup
sudo chmod 700 /etc/cron.hourly/sys_cleanup
```

To monitor the execution cycle to confirm it runs, you can check the cron logs manually:
```bash
grep CRON /var/log/syslog | grep sys_cleanup
```
